v0.0.3.10 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **The FATE grind no longer starts FATEs above your level.** Level sync only lowers your level to match a FATE, it never raises it, so a FATE above your level could not be contributed to and walking to it only wasted time. - Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.9 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Display name format and sort order changes are now saved.** Edits in the FATE tracker's "Sorting & Display" settings previously lived only in memory and reverted on the next plugin load; every change now persists immediately.
- **Reset to Default restores the actual default sort order.** The reset button dropped the Time Remaining criterion and put Time Remaining Urgent in ascending order (urgent FATEs last); it now restores the shipped six-entry default, shared with the config's own default so the two cannot drift apart.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.8 (2026-10-13) [testing]

- **The grind no longer clears a BossMod preset another plugin (such as AutoDuty) or the player set.** It turns its preset on and off with BossMod Reborn's standard preset calls and only ever clears its own. Two calls BossMod Reborn does not provide, which failed on every attempt, are gone, and a failing call is logged once per run.
- The BossMod preset named "Gluttony" that earlier versions created is no longer used. It is left untouched in BossMod's preset list and can be deleted there by hand.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.0.3.7 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The boss FATE icon on the server info bar entry now actually renders.** The previous testing build showed no icon at all because the glyph reference pointed at an empty slot instead of the boss FATE icon; the icon value is now pinned so it stays the boss glyph.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Click behavior, the confirming second click and every other part of the server bar entry are unchanged.

v0.0.3.6 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The server info bar entry shows the boss FATE icon instead of the sword glyphs.** The same icon is used in every state; the bot's on/off state stays in the text (": On", ": Off" and the rest), exactly as before. No other entry is affected.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

{"Author":"GitHixy","Name":"HitSpark","Punchline":"Replace the game's combat numbers with animated, styleable fly text.","Description":"HitSpark replaces Final Fantasy XIV's combat text with its own renderer: better fonts, tuned motion and real impact on critical hits.

WHAT YOU GET

- Every kind of combat text redrawn: damage dealt and taken, healing, misses and evades, status effects, experience, crafting and loot.
- Eight built-in presets, each a complete look: Classic+, Heroic, Tally, Onslaught, Elemental, Grim, Minimal and Retro.
- Real motion: arcs, fountains, rising and falling paths, scrolling columns, and punch, shake, flash, sparks and trails on crits.
- Multi-hits and damage over time that roll up into one number, with DoT ticks in their own colour.
- Other players' numbers shown smaller, or hidden, for your party and for everyone else.
- A style editor for every category with a live preview, and presets you can share as a short code.

GETTING STARTED

Type /hitspark (or /hs) to open the settings and pick a preset. /hitspark test plays sample numbers on you and your target, even out of combat.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you.

PLAYS BY THE RULES

HitSpark is purely cosmetic: it only redraws text the game already shows you and follows the game's own flying text and pop-up text options. {"Author":"GitHixy","Name":"FateLimit","Punchline":"See the edge of every FATE, and know before you step out of it.","Description":"FateLimit draws the border of FATE areas right in the world, so you always know where the fight ends and never lose your level sync by wandering out.

WHAT YOU GET

- Five border styles made to sit in Eorzea: Aether ring, Barrier wall, Marching dashes, Crystal runes and FATE ember.
- Two ways to show them: always, or only when you get close to the edge of the FATE you're in.
- A warning colour that creeps in as you near the edge, an on-screen banner with the distance left and a marker on the closest point of the border.
- Borders that follow the ground over hills and slopes instead of floating through them.
- Colour, thickness, height, spacing, glow and animation for every style, with a live preview in the settings.

GETTING STARTED

{"Author":"DhogGPT","Name":"Deep Ducking","Punchline":"Deep Ducking public host and authenticated module access.","Description":"The Deep Ducking public host provides the introduction, community links and authenticated loading of separately supplied DDuck modules. /deepducking and /dduck open the introduction when no module is loaded.

Commands (use /deepducking; /dduck is an alias):
/deepducking [toggle main window]
/dduck [alias for /deepducking; accepts all commands below]
/deepducking mini [toggle Mini]
/deepducking settings [open Settings]
/deepducking config [open Settings]
/deepducking debug [reveal and open Advanced for this plugin load]
/deepducking help [open command help]
/deepducking start [floor] [start or continue selected save; optional fresh-run floor]
/deepducking party-start [floor] [alias for start]
/deepducking party [select fixed-party POTD while idle]
/deepducking adopt [bind eligible already-entered party dungeon]
/deepducking hold [pause local output; retain run for Resume]
/deepducking resume [resume retained local run after readiness checks]
/deepducking nextstop [exit after next boss]
/deepducking ns [exit after next boss]
/deepducking stop [FULL STOP; persist local lock across reloads; stay in duty]
/deepducking reset-stop [clear eligible FULL STOP after cleanup; do not start]
/deepducking status [print local status]
/deepducking inspect [record read-only client and native observations]
/deepducking saves [open Saves]
/deepducking saves info <dungeon> [inspect native saves]
/deepducking saves delete <dungeon> <1|2> [delete selected save after native checks; no extra confirmation]
/deepducking saves dof <dungeon> <1|2> <on|off> [set future-failure deletion preference; no deletion now]
/deepducking saves cancel [cancel pending save or Start preparation; completed actions remain]

Dungeon arguments: potd, hoh, eo, pt. [floor] is optional; <...> is required. Choose one value for 1|2 or on|off; omit brackets when typing. {"Author":"dexcss","Name":"Glamour Sorter","AcceptsFeedback":true,"ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.3.0.19","CategoryTags":["Utility","Inventory"],"Changelog":"v1.3.0.19: Spare copies are no longer planned as stores — a piece whose appearance is already in the dresser is dropped from the set plan and reported as a duplicate (the bag copy can be sold), which also removes the HQ leftovers that made the game refuse outfit stores. Skipped sets are always reported now (1.3.0.18 dropped them from the result list), and the plan card note text is fixed. v1.3.0.18: Outfit stores now hand in NQ pieces only — every HQ hand-in made the game refuse the combination silently (all successful stores in the 21:15-21:30 run used NQ pieces, all refusals involved HQ). HQ-only sets are reported as \"the dresser will not take HQ gear as an outfit glamour\" instead of failing after a click. Slot diagnostics also show each planned piece's quality. v1.3.0.17: Failed outfit stores now report the game's own reason — chat messages printed during the attempt are logged under \"game said:\" and the result reads \"The game did not accept this outfit (left for manual review)\", so the remaining refusals can be identified exactly instead of guessed. v1.3.0.16: Confirmation now clicks the real Yes button first (what a player does), then falls back to callback event 2 and event 0 in stages — the seasonal dialog was closing without depositing when only callbacks were fired. Combined with 1.3.0.15, \"already in the stored outfit\" is reported as ALREADY and is no longer counted as a store. v1.3.0.15: Honest results — \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" is now its own ALREADY state and no longer counts as a successful store; the tally reads stored / already there / need attention / failed. The store step also logs the click and, if no confirmation opens within 2 s, fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) before giving up. v1.3.0.14: Diagnosis + fallback for the seasonal Outfit Glamour Creation stalls — the store step now logs the addon state, hand-in counts and every slot (item id, inventory type, flag), and if no confirmation opens within 2 s it fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) as a fallback. v1.3.0.13: Quality consistency for outfit hand-ins — the outfit window only accepts pieces of one quality (\"Only items of the same quality may be selected\") and a mixed HQ/NQ selection made the game silently refuse the store while leaving the window open. The plugin now anchors on the quality it holds most of and hands in only pieces of that quality, logging any piece skipped for quality. v1.3.0.12: Checkbox-dialog fix — the confirm ladder now ticks the \"Store as Outfit Glamour\" checkbox first (synthetic ButtonClick + SetChecked) and fires Yes once the game enables it, instead of firing the default-confirm callback first, which closed the dialog without depositing on several sets (the \"checkbox was never selected\" symptom). The default-confirm callback is kept as a fallback for dialogs whose Yes cannot be enabled from the checkbox. v1.3.0.11: Cross-set outfit mismatch guard — a glamour piece can belong to more than one outfit set, and the game may open a different set's stored outfit when completing; the plugin now compares the opened outfit's item id with the planned set and skips with \"left for manual review\" instead of handing the piece into the wrong outfit and reporting a false failure. The store log keeps the dialog mode and prism-box index so any remaining case is diagnosable. v1.3.0.10: Fix the \"No deposit detected\" failures on outfit completions. The hand-in loop was allowed to target a slot already marked Filled (the outfit already contained that piece), which the game silently refused; it now only hands into Unfilled slots, and a set whose planned pieces are all already inside the outfit reports \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" instead of attempting a store. The native StoreExistingOutfit retry from 1.3.0.9 is removed — it returns success but deposits nothing unless the Glamour Creation window drives it. v1.3.0.9: Fix false \"No deposit detected\" results when completing an outfit — the game's confirm dialog sometimes closes without depositing for outfits that were only just created. After 1.5 s without a change the plugin now sends the same request the dialog sends (StoreExistingOutfit/StoreNewOutfit) once, then re-checks; store logs also report the dialog mode and prism-box index for diagnosis. v1.3.0.8: Withdraw tab clarity — the action buttons now state what they will do and grey out with an explicit empty-state label: \"No duplicates to withdraw\", \"No singles to withdraw\", and \"No sets to withdraw & re-deposit\" when there is nothing to pack (otherwise \"Withdraw & re-deposit sets (N)\" with counts). The consolidation description now explains the withdraw-then-pack-as-outfit loop and the slot saving. v1.3.0.7: Fix a window render crash when the set-consolidation loop ran with no loose set pieces left to start (the empty candidate list was indexed directly) — it now reports \"Nothing to consolidate\" instead. The consolidation pump is also exception-guarded so a future error cannot take the whole window down. v1.3.0.6: Set consolidation now runs in bag-sized batches — it withdraws one set's loose pieces (only as many as your free bag slots can hold), stores that set as a single outfit glamour, then repeats automatically. Before this the button tried to withdraw every loose set piece at once (359 items against 63 free slots) and was refused. v1.3.0.5: Dresser-full handling — at 800/800 the store run now stops with a clear 'Glamour Dresser is full' result instead of failing every remaining item with 'no deposit detected'. New \"set pieces stored loose\" detector on the Withdraw tab: it finds items the dresser stores individually that belong to an outfit set, shows how many pieces/sets and the approximate slots that would be freed, withdraws them (arm-then-confirm), then automatically runs the store pass that packs each set into one outfit glamour. v1.3.0.4: Single-item deposits now work — loose glamour items (not part of an outfit set) are stored with the game's own prism-box request command (the same request the Glamour Creation window's Yes button sends) instead of trying to open the outfit-store window, which the game only opens for set items. Each item costs one glamour prism (checked first) and the result reports \"Stored item (dresser X->Y)\". Outfit sets keep the existing flow. v1.3.0.3: Withdraw fix — the extractor was waiting on the dresser's 'requested' flag, which stays set while the data is loaded, so a run could stop before sending anything (\"the dresser data stayed busy\"); it now only gates on the loaded flag and retries refused sends. Store: the hand-in window is allowed to finish populating before the fill step decides nothing can be handed over. UI: two pages — Deposit (scan/store) and Withdraw (extractor) — with Abort reachable on the active page. v1.3.0.2: Gear-set protection hardening — items saved in a gear set are now detected from the saved gearset entries as well as the game's gear-set icon check (a 1.3.0.0 test scan saw 110 protected pieces on one pass and only 1 on another, so a piece could be misfiled as sortable). Deposit verification now reads the dresser list from MirageManager, so a dresser window that is momentarily unreadable no longer turns a successful deposit into a false \"couldn't read the dresser\" warning. v1.3.0.1: Fixes from the first 1.3.0.0 test. The dresser's \"Add to pre-existing outfit glamour?\" Yes/No prompt (shown when completing a stored outfit) is now answered automatically — before this it left the store flow stuck with the prompt on screen and froze the run. The Abort button stays clickable while a run is in progress. New watchdogs stop a set whose store window never opens or never produces its confirmation instead of stalling the rest of the run. Extractor: a refused RestorePrismBoxItem is retried (the client briefly refuses while a previous restore settles), waits for the dresser data request to finish, and skips further copies of a unique item (the game cannot give you a second copy while you hold one) instead of stopping the whole run; log lines now name the refused item. v1.3.0.0: Loose items — glamour-able items that belong to no outfit set are now stored as well, one at a time, and skipped when that item is already anywhere in the dresser. Extractor — withdraw dresser items back into your bags: all loose items, duplicates only (keeps one of each), or one item or item type such as all rings, with a live progress line. Item names and icons — planned pieces, duplicates and results now show the item icon, name and category instead of a raw item id. v1.2.0.1: Audit fixes. Completing an existing outfit works again — the pieces a stored outfit is still missing are planned as needed and are no longer listed as sellable duplicates. Deposit verification also accepts the planned pieces leaving your bags, so completing an outfit (or storing with a nearly full dresser) reports correctly instead of \"No deposit detected\". Store steps can no longer drop a set silently when a window does not open or the dresser closes mid-run, the store loop retries briefly while the dresser data reloads instead of stopping the rest of the run, and the Armoire toggle is locked while storing. /xllog now logs the scanned dresser/held counts for troubleshooting. v1.2.0.0: Full audit. Gear-set protection — pieces registered to a saved gear set are now left in your bags (the same check the game uses for its gear-set icon mark), instead of being pulled out of your gear sets. Smarter duplicates — stored outfit glamours are expanded into their pieces, so a second copy of an already-stored piece is flagged as sellable instead of being re-stored. The dresser's expanded item list is scanned, and a never-fill guard skips window slots the game already marks as part of the stored outfit. New model-duplicate hints show when a planned piece shares its appearance with something already stored. Deposit verification now retries briefly instead of failing on a single read. UI: version in the title, live progress tally while storing, MANUAL tag priority, gear-set and model-duplicate sections. Removed diagnostic logging. v1.1.1.0: The Store as Outfit Glamour checkbox dialog is now automated (synthetic checkbox click + default-confirm callback); all sets route to the dresser. v1.1.0.0: Armoire routing added.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Sorts glamour-able gear from your inventory into the Glamour Dresser — outfit sets as outfit glamours (including seasonal sets, with the Store as Outfit Glamour checkbox dialog automated) and loose items one by one — skipping anything already stored. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.324","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v1.0.4.332 (2026-11-05) [testing]
- **A party-callout reader that joins chat words to the live fight state, log only (Jev Fight Brain).** While in combat inside a duty, short party and alliance chat lines from party members are read and joined to the exact state the plugin already sees: the head-marker signs each member carries, who is tethered, where the members stand relative to the player, the Fight Brain forecast's next mechanic with its countdown, how long ago the last mechanic resolved, and who said the line. The code builds a few candidate responses from that state first (one marker means that player; two markers mean the player's own light party's marker under the role-split arrangement; no marker with a stack forecast within six seconds means pre-position; no marker and nothing soon means the line is stale and nothing moves; a telegraph under the player outranks every callout) and computes the code's own answer. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"PvP Solver","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.1.2","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"- **The Jev co-pilot logs the plain code rule's answer beside Jev's, for both of its questions.** Each `JV|focus-pick` line names the enemy Jev picked and the enemy the plain rule would pick (the lowest-HP enemy in attack range); each `JV|lb-shadow` line names Jev's Limit Break call and the code rule's. Both answers are recorded side by side and graded after the session, to show which one decides better. Log only: targeting, Limit Break firing and every other behavior are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- Upstream engine sync (RotationSolverReborn a560469db): the rotation engine now builds in upstream's merged single-project layout.
- Ports upstream engine fixes: the action manager is read at call time instead of a pointer cached at startup (a stale-pointer crash class), configuration saves are atomic (write to a temp file, then replace), and the shield-value calculation can no longer overflow on very large HP values.
- No rotation behavior change; the 21 PvP rotations and their presets are untouched.

v0.1.2.10 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **The per-job defensive actions also read real HP.** Heart of Corundum, Tempera Coat, Earth's Reply, Riddle of Earth, the Bloodbath rows, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui, Impalement, Xenoglossy's low-HP arm and Shadowbringer's HP arm compared their "use below this HP" thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP. They now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value Guard and the defensive table already use. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged, and reads of enemies' and allies' HP (Smite, Guardian, Blasting Zone, Perfectio, the burst target) are untouched.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.9 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **Self-defence now reads real HP.** Guard, Recuperate and the generic defensive actions (the "use below X% HP" table) compared their thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP, so nothing fired. All of them now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value the Jev snapshot uses. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.8 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" now sees real HP.** The player's and allies' HP sent to Jev is the current HP out of the maximum, no longer PvP Solver's predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way. In one match Jev was told 84% one second before a death at about 40%.
- **Jev's pick no longer drops when Jev is briefly unsure.** The relay now keeps the last pick itself while that enemy is still hittable, and drops it on purpose when the enemy goes under Guard, out of reach or stale. PvP Solver follows the relay's call and never brings a dropped pick back. Only with an older relay does PvP Solver keep the last pick, for up to three seconds after Jev gave it, while that enemy is still a valid target.
- **The Limit Break log matches what happened.** `JV|lb-fired` is written once when the Limit Break goes off in a fire window. `JV|lb-fire-skip` is written only when a window closes without it, with the reason: unusable, follow-up, out-of-range, no-target or timeout. A report of the use that arrives up to two seconds late still counts as fired. Before, a skip line could appear in windows that then fired, and windows that really failed wrote nothing.
- **Each action used is reported once.** The game reports each action twice; the same action on the same target within 1.5 seconds now counts once in the snapshot.
- **Alliance members are included (Frontline).** After the party members, the nearest alliance members are sent too, marked as alliance, up to eight allies in all. Each ally now carries its object id, so Jev can name an ally to heal.
- **Healer call, logged only.** When Jev suggests whom a healer should heal (an ally, self, attack or Guard), the suggestion is written as one `JV|heal-shadow` log line for the first suggestion in each fight and each time it changes; an answer with no suggestion does not count as a change. Nothing acts on it yet.
- **Relay failures are visible in the log.** One summary line per fight (when combat ends, or every 60 seconds while calls fail) counts calls that succeeded, timed out, got an error reply or failed. No line per call, and no call is counted in a later fight. An unreadable heal or Limit Break value in a reply no longer drops the rest of the answer.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.7 (2026-10-29) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" reports what actually happened.** Each snapshot also carries the player's current target and the actions actually used since the last one (action and target only), so each of Jev's picks can be checked against what PvP Solver did and whether that enemy went down.
- Jev's focus pick is kept steady: it moves to another enemy only when that one is clearly the better pick.
- **A line, cone or splash Limit Break that Jev called could be skipped** because the action kept its own "most enemies" target. It is now aimed at the enemy Jev chose, which the game has just confirmed as a valid target. A skipped fire writes one reason line to the log.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.6 (2026-10-29) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" now fires the PvP Limit Break.** When the Limit Break is ready, Jev is asked about this job's own Limit Break (what it does, from the game's description) with the facts that decide it: the damage against each enemy's remaining HP, Guard, Kuzushi and low-HP executes, how many enemies a line, cone or area would catch, and which allies are hurt or under attack. It fires when that wins a kill, catches several enemies, or saves the player or an ally, and holds otherwise. Only enemies the game says the Limit Break can be used on right now are offered, and the game is asked again just before firing.
- The focus pick also weighs each enemy's remaining HP and how many allies are already attacking it.
- With the setting off, or the relay slow or down, no Limit Break is fired (as before).

- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the "Sit while fishing" switch to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-25)

- Persistent seating across fishing hole visits: if the character stands up during a visit to a fishing hole (such as putting the rod away to change bait or use cordials, or manually standing up), the automation now detects the stand and re-seats upon resuming fishing or on the subsequent cast.
- Unaccepted send cap: the 3-send limit per hole visit is now scoped to consecutive unaccepted sends rather than a lifetime cap per hole visit. When a sit is accepted by the game, the counter resets, ensuring long fishing sessions with multiple bait changes or pauses remain seated while still guarding against unbounded retry loops if commands are blocked.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-25)

- Sits after a cast: the automated /sit check now runs after a cast once the line is settled in the water (`LineInWater`), in addition to the pre-cast standby beat (`PoleReady`). In active fishing loops or when using automated casting tools, the standby beat between casts typically lasts under a second, which previously prevented the automation from ever triggering across repeated casts (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- Safe timing: commands are sent only after the line has been in the water for at least 1 second to ensure the cast animation has resolved, and continue to be refused during active casting, biting, hooking, reeling, and position change animations.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Correction first, because the last release's notes got the game wrong: FFXIV does NOT force standing on every hooked fish. If the character is sitting when the cast starts, the game keeps it seated for the whole loop - a hook may cause a momentary stand, but the game sits back down on its own. v0.1.2.0 was designed around that mistake (one /sit per cast) and this release replaces it entirely.
- Sit once, then stay out of the way. The plugin now sends a single /sit per fishing trip, at a moment the game will actually accept it, and then does nothing for the rest of the trip (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`).
- That moment is the standby beat: rod out, no line in the water (`FishingEventHandler.State == PoleReady`), held for a second, at least 3 seconds clear of a bite/hook/reel, with the character read as standing for 3 seconds straight. It will never fire mid-cast, with a line in the water, mid-bite, mid-reel, or while already sitting down or standing up (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- That is why v0.1.1.0 looked like it did nothing: it sent its one /sit the instant the fishing flag came on, which is after the line is already out, and the game swallows the emote there - ten sends across ten sessions, no effect. v0.1.2.0 still counted "line in water" as a valid moment and would have done the same thing.
- No re-sit after every cast, ever. A brief standing read just after a bite, hook, reel or collectable prompt is treated as the game's own animation, not as the character standing up, so the plugin does nothing and lets the game re-seat (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsHookish`).
- A "trip" is one visit to a fishing hole, not one cast. The fishing flag drops between casts (v0.1.1.0 saw ten "sessions" in 21 minutes), so the limits are now anchored to the hole and only reset after 20 seconds away from it (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `StartTrip` / `EndTrip`).
- Anti-yo-yo guards, all hard, because a /sit on a seated character STANDS them: never sends while any seated signal reads seated; at least 10 seconds between sends; at most 3 sends per trip with a log line when it stops; and once the game has taken a sit this trip it will not send again unless the seated read has proved it still reports seated with the rod out (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`, guards 1-5).
- The settings window now shows the trip counters: whether the character is at a hole, sits used out of 3, whether the game took the sit, and whether the seated read works while fishing (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`).
- Removed the "check interval" slider. The plugin now looks every frame, because every limit that matters is a real time limit (10 seconds between sends, 3 seconds of standing before it believes the read, 3 sends a trip) and a 2-second poll just made it step over short standby beats between quick casts. Saved values are ignored, not lost (files: `ConfigWindow.cs`, `Configuration.cs`).
- The policy is now a plain C# class with no game code in it (`Core/SitPolicy.cs`), replayed offline against 26 scripted fishing sessions by `tests/LazyFishSitter.Harness`. Three releases in a row shipped a rule that only broke in game; the harness caught three more before this one shipped, including a dead window that would have stopped a refused /sit from ever being retried.
- Keeps the detailed state logging (every fishing-state and posture change, 40 lines a minute max) and adds a one-line trip summary, so the still-open question - does the game ever report seated while a line is out - can be answered from the log without typing anything in game (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `EndTrip`).

v0.1.2.0 (2026-09-05)

- SUPERSEDED BY v0.1.3.0 AND NEVER FISHED ON: the design premise below was wrong. It claimed the game forces standing on every hooked fish; it does not - if the character was sitting before the hook, the game re-seats automatically. Everything in this entry that follows from that premise (a /sit per stand episode) was removed in v0.1.3.0. Kept here for the record only.
- Re-sat after every cast and every catch, on the mistaken premise above: the unit was a "stand episode" (fishing start, or the fishing state machine passing through Hooking/ReleasingCatch/ConfirmingCollectable), and each episode got at most ONE /sit (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Arm` / `TrackTransitions`).
- Sent only when it believed the game would accept it: read `EventFramework.Instance()->EventHandlerModule.FishingEventHandler` (FFXIVClientStructs) and required `State` to be `PoleReady` or `LineInWater` for at least 1 s with `ChangingPosition` false. Counting `LineInWater` as acceptable was the second defect - that is exactly where the emote gets swallowed (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Tick`).
- Proof the sit took: `FishingEventHandler.ChangingPosition` going true within 3 s of the send was logged as `game accepted our sit`, with a 3 s outcome line per send. This part was correct and is kept in v0.1.3.0 (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `TrackTransitions`).
- No detector-driven re-arm: a "not seated" read after a sit never triggered a re-send on its own (that is what yo-yoed v0.1.0.0). Also kept in v0.1.3.0, hardened (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Tick`).
- Logged every posture/fishing state CHANGE at Information, rate-limited to 40 lines/min: Fishing flag, FishingState, ChangingPosition, CanFish, Character.Mode/ModeParam, EmoteController.EmoteId, GetPosture(), and the combined SEATED verdict (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `TrackTransitions`, `LogTransition`).
- A failing FFXIVClientStructs signature (EventFramework or GetPosture) is logged once at Warning instead of being swallowed silently every check (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Read`).
- Added the shared in-game "What's new" popup (repo standing rule): after an update this changelog opens once; `/lazyfishsitter changelog` reopens it (files: `Plugin.cs`, `Configuration.cs` `LastSeenChangelogVersion`, `LazyFishSitter.csproj` compiles `src/Shared/LalaChangelog`).","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/tree/main/src/LazyFishSitter","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":false,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/releases/download/LazyFishSitter-v0.1.5.1/LazyFishSitter.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/releases/download/LazyFishSitter-v0.1.5.1/LazyFishSitter.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/releases/download/LazyFishSitter-v0.1.5.2/LazyFishSitter-testing.zip","Tags":["fishing","lazy","sit","emote","utility"],"CategoryTags":["utility"],"IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/LalaImages/lazyfishsitter-icon.png","ImageUrls":[""],"DownloadCount":0,"LastUpdate":"0","_SourceId":"dajoey-lalalazy","_SourceName":"dajoey / lalalazy","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/pluginmaster.json","_Category":"crafting"}

- **The overlay buttons no longer have to cover the retainer windows' own controls.** The Auto Pinch, Auto Market and Sweep to Bags buttons are pinned to the top-right corner of the retainer list and retainer sell list windows, where they can cover the venture currency and the windows' close button (reported in issue #12). v0.2.8.16 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Fresh installs no longer show an import notice for a plugin that was never installed.** A leftover line in the configuration loader set the "imported from Dagobert Price Matcher" flag true on every load that created a new configuration, so a brand-new install showed the import notice and the uninstall hint even though no settings were ever imported. The flag now keeps its false default; a genuine import from a found Dagobert configuration still sets it, and the load log's imported= field reports the real value.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.15 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **The Auto-Market panel's two filter dropdowns remember their setting between sessions.** The status filter (every stack / on the list / not on the list / excluded) and the market-category filter used to reset to "every stack, every category" every time the plugin loaded or the game restarted; they now save as soon as they are changed and come back that way. A saved category the current bags do not contain still shows as "every category" instead of silently hiding everything, and the saved choice comes back when the bags hold that category again.
- Untried build: tested offline against a saved-configuration round trip (the plugin's offline test suite), not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.14 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **A pinch row that cannot get its dialog or its price is now skipped; it no longer aborts the whole retainer with the price dialog left open.** Each row step waits for a dialog or a market price. When one never arrived, the wait ran into the task manager's hard 10-second limit, which discards every remaining task of the run and leaves the dialog on screen. Each row step now has a shorter budget of its own: when it runs out, the row is skipped with a log line naming the stage and row, the row's dialogs are closed, any late market reply is dropped, and the run carries on with the next row. A skipped row keeps its current price.
- **A Universalis timeout is no longer mistaken for a cancellation.** The sale-history lookup used when the market board is empty (and the data-center price lookup) swallowed the HTTP client's own 8-second timeout as if the run had been cancelled, so no answer was ever delivered and the row waited out the hard limit. A timeout is now reported as a failed lookup ("Universalis did not answer in time") and the row falls back to the normal no-price handling.
- **The empty-board sale-history wait now actually times out.** Its 6-second deadline could never be reached because the pending candidate price was cleared on every retry; the candidate is now kept while the lookup is pending.
- **A run that does stop (a step timeout, a session cap, a vendoring halt) closes what it left open before AutoRetainer is handed back.** The price dialog, item menu, market result, sell list and retainer inventory panel are closed innermost-first within a few seconds, the retainer menu is left for AutoRetainer, and the buyback-abandon confirm is never touched. The log names the last stage and what was closed.
- **The AutoRetainer session cap grows with the number of rows the session queued** instead of staying a flat five minutes, so a long pinch list at slow market-board delays is not cut off.
- **A manual sweep that reaches a retainer's buyback-abandon confirm now parks there with a plain report** instead of letting the next retainer's click wait out the hard limit and abort with a generic timeout. The report names the retainers that did not run.
- **An interrupted manual sweep can be resumed.** Starting the sweep again within 30 minutes runs only the retainers that had not finished; retainers that finished are not re-priced.
- Untried build: the guard was tested offline against a simulated task chain and the plugin source, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.13 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **The Auto-Market panel's confirmation dialogs open now.** In 0.2.8.12, "Add all visible", "Remove all visible" and the panel's Enable Auto-Market switch each tried to show a confirmation dialog under a different name than the one they opened it with, so no dialog could ever appear and those controls did nothing when clicked. The names now match, and a regression test scans the panel's code so a button and its dialog cannot drift apart silently again.
- Correction to 0.2.8.12's notes: the panel's Enable Auto-Market switch asks for confirmation before turning Auto-Market on. That confirmation is the panel's own safety - the main window's switch has never had one, and 0.2.8.12's notes wrongly implied it did.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.12 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **A new Auto-Market panel window lists every marketable stack in your bags and whether it is on the Auto-Market list** - the same two states the bag dots mark (plus what a dot cannot show: entries whose tick is unticked, and the quick-exclude flag), as a table with quantities. Each row has quick Add/Remove, and entries expose the same stack-size, keep-in-bags and skip-routing edits as the main window's table. The panel covers your four bag containers, which is what Auto-Market's bags stock source draws from.
- **"Add all visible" / "Remove all visible" add or remove exactly the rows the filters currently show**, with the count on the button and a confirmation dialog before anything changes.
- **The panel carries the global Auto-Market knobs** in a collapsible section: master switch, markers, AutoRetainer, stock source, pricing, reserve slots, pinch behaviour, listing order, the value gate and auto-assign - the same controls as the Auto-Market tab, writing the same settings. What the main window does not expose is not exposed here either. The master switch keeps its confirmation on turning on and stays locked while a run is in progress.
- **Status filters, a name search, a category filter, and an optional count of unmarketable stacks** (hidden by default, like the dots' "no dot at all"). On-list rows keep the list's own order; everything else sorts by name. The panel never fetches prices, so the price-based listing orders are not applied here.
- **The panel docks beside the inventory window**: to its right when the screen has room, else to its left, else it floats at a position it remembers (clamped on screen, so it can never drift out of reach). It opens with the inventory, closes with it unless pinned, and `/lmc panel` toggles it any time. An inventory window that cannot be read is just the floating case - the panel always appears, and the plugin log's open line carries the dock mode, position, size, the inventory rectangle and scale it read, and the row counts.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyCrafter","Punchline":"What can I make right now, what's it worth, and what would it take to make the rest?","Description":"Catalogs every recipe you can craft, buckets them by how much effort the missing materials take, prices them with Universalis, and hands the missing-material work to Artisan / GBR / ARC / Lifestream.","InternalName":"LazyCrafter","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.7.8","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.7.9","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"Changelog":"v0.1.7.9 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Market-price lookups no longer log warnings while they retry.** When Universalis is slow or busy it answers with a temporary "try again" status or takes longer than before; the price client already retries those on its own with a pause between tries - that is its designed behavior, not a fault, so those lines now go to the debug log. Only one warning is written when a batch gives up entirely after all retries, and stale cached prices are used meanwhile, exactly as before.
- **The price client now waits up to 60 seconds per request instead of 20.** Under load, Universalis sometimes finishes a large price query just after the old 20-second cutoff; the request was cancelled while the server was still working on it and the prices for that batch were refetched from scratch. The longer budget lets those queries land.
- Market-price log lines no longer paste a hundred item numbers into the log; a batch is described as its item count instead.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 401/401 PASS (6 new).

v0.1.7.8 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Knightshopper no longer buys units that are sitting on a retainer.** The purchase target counted everything the catalog can see, but the fetch-from-retainer step runs after the purchase and brings those units in anyway - with 90 units on a retainer, none in the bags and 9 missing, the run bought 99 instead of 9. The target now counts what is physically in the bags, and the fetch tops the bags up to exactly what the cart needs; every currency routes on the same corrected target.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Full harness: 395/395 PASS (4 new).

v0.1.7.7 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Cart dispatches can hand vendor purchases to Knightshopper.** When a dispatch is missing materials that a vendor sells - gil vendors, and currency vendors priced in one currency Knightshopper supports - the run groups that list by currency and buys it through Knightshopper's purchase IPC at target inventory totals, before any shopping stop fires. The run prints each group, its currency and the estimated total cost before anything is spent. Market-board items are never routed, and one attempt per group means a refused purchase never retries; a repeat dispatch asks for the same target totals at most, so nothing is ever bought twice.
- If Knightshopper is missing, busy, refuses LazyCrafter, or has no unlocked vendor for an item, those items fall back to the usual shopping stops - flagged and named in chat exactly as before. Purchases also need LazyCrafter on Knightshopper's allowed-plugins IPC list, which is set in Knightshopper's own settings (IPC permissions); LazyCrafter never changes Knightshopper's settings. The new switch (on by default) is "Buy vendor items through Knightshopper during a dispatch" in the settings.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the switch off, or without Knightshopper installed, the run behaves exactly as before.
- Full harness: 391/391 PASS (16 new).

v0.1.7.6 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the catalog and price settings (recipes above the character's level, the undersupplied thresholds, the revenue basis, pricing at the home world only, the price refresh interval, the price-match message) and the cart-run hand-off switches (fetching materials from retainers, walking to a summoning bell or to vendors, preferring a currency shop) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The cart-run hand-off switches can only be changed while no cart run is active.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.7.5 (2026-09-16)

- **The shopping-stop Resume popup window is gone.** The 0.1.7.4 test pass: the full-screen popup opened at every shopping stop sat over the game and blocked mouse input with the client - verdict: remove the resume extra window. The window is removed and nothing else changed: a blocked shopping stop still says the what-to-do message in chat and on the Run tab exactly once, and Resume stays on the Run tab button, in chat (/lcraft resume) and the copied report - keyboard-only resume works

v0.1.7.4 (2026-09-15)

{"Author":"Bronya Rand","Name":"Things To Do In Eorzea","Punchline":"Unsure what to do? Forgot what you wanted to do? Nonsense! There's always things to do in Eorzea!","Description":"
Keep track of all your objectives and tasks in Eorzea. Whether it's collecting tomes/items/gear, completing dungeons/trials/raids, FATEs, or purely making a random list of things to do to keep yourself busy, keep yourself organized and on track with this plugin.

Features:
    - Create and manage a list of objectives and tasks.
    - Automatically track your progress on objectives and tasks.
    - View your objectives and tasks with a window inspired by the in-game Duty Log.
    - Automatic translation of objectives and tasks to your game client's language. (No need to write what you want to do. Just setup how you want to do it and the plugin will fill in the rest!)
    - Open creativity for just about anything that comes up to mine! (...What? You don't think making silly challenges like doing Endsinger's Aria - Extreme with MINE in under 12 minutes a good idea? Seriously, you can make that a task if you want)
       
Inspired by the idea of "DYOM" (Design Your Own Mission) and "TTDISA" (Things To Do In San Andreas) from GTA: San Andreas as well as Simple To-Do List and other similar plugins.
    ","Changelog":"# What's New?
- Fixed a bug for items where the wrong item ID got displayed.","TestingChangelog":"Things To Do In Eorzea is more than just a simple to-do-list. It's one that automatically monitors what you need to collect, what duties you need to clear, FATEs and more! You can either set it up to track items you need or have it track your clears. Think that's not enough? You can even set yourself up some ridiculous tasks for yourself like doing MINE Bahamut or a whole Savage round without dying/wiping to just simply forcing yourself to play a specific job, or speedrun. There are always things to do in Eorzea. Just get creative!

Unlike other to-do plugins, Things To Do In Eorzea:
1. Auto-tracks your completed dungeons, trials and raids.
2. Auto-tracks your completed FATEs by region, a specific FATE or any FATE in general.
3. Auto-tracks the items in your inventory, making sure you have what you needed to get.
4. Make self-imposed challenges like doing Minstrel's Ballads on MINE difficulty, speedrun a Dungeon, one-shot/no kill, and more.
5. Read objectives in your native language*

   > French is partially broken ATM pending a Dalamud merge.

And you still have your sticky note for whenever you need it.

AI Use: Assist
> AI was used to inquire about translations from English to Japanese to show there was at least an attempt to show that localization is supported. However said translations may not be accurate. Anyone interested may PR or DM me their translated findings for German, Japanese and French if they so please. Thus far:
> - Full English on UI and Objective Display
> - Full Japanese [Claude+Gemini+Google Translate+DeepL+Japanese Dictionary] on UI and Objective Display
> - German only on the Objective Display with partial assistance from XIV community for macros and Claude
> - French only on the Objective DIsplay with assistance from Gemini and Clause
> 
> There was also AI assist for the localization system.","Tags":["to-do","list","track","task","objective","custom","utility","ui","other"],"CategoryTags":["utility","ui","other"],"IsHide":true,"InternalName":"ThingsToDoInEorzea","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.1.1","TestingAssemblyVersion":"1.0.0.0","IsTestingExclusive":false,"RepoUrl":"https://github.com/Bronya-Rand/ThingsToDoInEorzea.git","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"DownloadCount":1779,"LastUpdate":1794028623,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://kamori.goats.dev/Plugin/Download/ThingsToDoInEorzea?isUpdate=False&isTesting=False&branch=api9&isDip17=True","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goatcorp/DalamudPlugins/api9/plugins/ThingsToDoInEorzea/latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://kamori.goats.dev/Plugin/Download/ThingsToDoInEorzea?isUpdate=False&isTesting=True&branch=api9&isDip17=True","LoadPriority":0,"ImageUrls":null,"IconUrl":null,"AcceptsFeedback":true,"FeedbackMessage":null,"FeedbackWebhook":null,"_isDip17Plugin":true,"_Dip17Channel":"testing-live"}
